purpose: small-scale pilot run to validate the benchmark harness (scripts, timing, sampling) before a full multi-round run

wsl.note: Two Ubuntu distros exist; the user selected 'Ubuntu' (26.04) as the wsl-* execution origin for this benchmark, not the default 'Ubuntu-22.04'.
wsl.note2: networkingMode=mirrored means a container's published port is reachable at http://localhost:PORT from Windows regardless of which side (Windows or WSL) started the container, so the load generator always targets localhost from the Windows host.

wipWslc.note: wip.exe and wslc.exe are Windows-native binaries; the wsl-wip config invokes them from WSL Ubuntu bash via WSL interop (confirmed working, including cwd translation for a wip.yml found via the interop-translated working directory). No wip.yml existed in the wip source repo itself (expected: it is wip's own source tree, not a project that uses wip).

benchmarkApp.description: Fixed-response Node.js HTTP server, no framework/dependencies, returns a small fixed JSON body on any GET.
benchmarkApp.sourceDir: benchmark/app (NTFS, under the wip git repo)
benchmarkApp.note: Same physical directory referenced by two path spellings, per the protocol's requirement that the primary comparison hold storage location constant and vary only the execution shell.
builtWith: wslc build (for wip configs, via wip build in the actual harness)

loadGenerator.tool: custom Node.js script (benchmark/scripts/load-gen.mjs), no external dependencies
loadGenerator.executionOrigin: always the Windows host PowerShell process, regardless of which config is under test
loadGenerator.method: N persistent keep-alive worker loops issuing sequential GETs for a fixed wall-clock duration
